title: Binary derived open descent for modules on a ringed topos
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a Grothendieck topos (a category of sheaves of sets on a small site), $R$ a commutative ring object of $\mathcal T$, and $D(\mathcal T,R)$ the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects (monomorphisms into the terminal object) whose union is $1$, and put $W=U\times V$. Write $\mathcal T/U$, $\mathcal T/V$, $\mathcal T/W$ for the slice topoi, $R_U,R_V,R_W$ for the restricted rings, and $j_Z^*$ for restriction to a slice. The exact extension-by-zero left adjoint is denoted $j_{Z!}$ and the derived right adjoint of restriction is denoted $Rj_{Z*}$, for $Z=U,V,W$.

(1) Given $A\in D(\mathcal T/U,R_U)$, $B\in D(\mathcal T/V,R_V)$ and an isomorphism $c:A|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}B|_W$, there exist $G\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ and isomorphisms $a:G|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, $b:G|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $b|_W=c\circ a|_W$. One may take $G$ in a distinguished triangle
$$G\longrightarrow Rj_{U*}A\oplus Rj_{V*}B\xrightarrow{(Rj_*c,-1)}Rj_{W*}(B|_W)\longrightarrow G[1],$$
where each component is the derived restriction-adjunction map, with $c$ applied in the first component. If $A,B$ have cohomology in a common interval $[a_0,b_0]$, so does $G$.

(2) For every $M\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ there is the natural distinguished open-cover triangle
$$j_{W!}(M|_W)\xrightarrow{(1,-1)}j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)\xrightarrow{(1,1)}M\longrightarrow j_{W!}(M|_W)[1].$$
The arrows are the canonical nested-open maps and the adjunction counits. Restriction and extension by zero here act termwise on complexes. No uniqueness of a gluing of arbitrary derived morphisms is asserted.
